result.title: Ruby: State-of-the-Art Potency Prediction across Discovery Regimes Using Learned Structural Representations
result.summary: Small-molecule drug discovery proceeds through repeated design-make-test-analyze cycles. The goal is often to maximize potency while keeping other properties within the ranges required for a viable therapeutic candidate. Compound prioritization places different demands on computational methods as drug discovery progresses from hit identification through hit-to-lead and lead optimization, with changing computational budgets and increasing amounts of on-target experimental data. We introduce Ruby, a Robust Universal Binding affinitY predictor that uses intermediate representations from the structural foundation model Pearl without requiring an explicit binding pose for every compound. Ruby is trained on proprietary data plus GenesisPotency-2026, an audited public-source potency training dataset released for academic and commercial use under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license with row-level provenance and audit annotations. Ruby achieves the highest aggregate early enrichment across seven public hit-identification targets among evaluated methods, with adjustable inference effort trading off enrichment and computational cost over more than two orders of magnitude. Ruby achieves the highest average correlations across four public benchmarks: OpenFE, CASP16, FEP+ 4, and OpenBind. Ruby significantly outperforms other methods in zero-shot prediction across eight biochemical and cellular assays from five ongoing Genesis-Incyte programs, widening its performance advantage relative to the public benchmarks. Ruby continues to improve more than other methods when all are given the opportunity to recalibrate using earlier assay measurements. Together, these contributions provide an annotated training resource for the field and a state-of-the-art potency predictor for broad screening, prioritization within related chemical series, and assay-specific prediction as experimental measurements accumulate.

AI.brief_summary: Ruby 是小分子效价预测器，复用结构基础模型 Pearl 的中间表示且不要求每个化合物有显式结合构象，同时发布带溯源与审计标注的公开训练数据集，并在多个公开基准和零样本实验中取得领先。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关联，但其可调推理开销在两个数量级上权衡富集率与计算成本、并随累积实验数据再校准，可为 THINK/STOP 的计算分配与停止决策评价提供远距离类比，机制是否可迁移可供核查。
